task: SEM particle SHAPE classification (fibre/bead/fragment) pilot -- NOT polymer classification
validity_warning: All three models below achieve near-identical, essentially perfect scores (~1.0 across accuracy/macro-F1/AUC on both val and test, and under every robustness perturbation tested). This should NOT be attributed to genuine shape-classification capability. Diagnostic work in evidence/public/sem_shape/data_leakage_notes.md shows each class is drawn from a small, near-disjoint set of source products/imaging sessions that is shared identically across train/val/test (e.g. bead = a single product/session in every split), so models can key on session-level nuisance signal (background, resolution, scale-bar/session artifacts) rather than particle morphology. A trivial RandomForest trained on ONLY [width, height, aspect_ratio] (no pixels) reaches 77% accuracy -- well above the 40% majority baseline but short of 100%, confirming dimensions are a partial but not sole confound; the remainder is attributed to the session confound. Zero exact-duplicate files were found across splits (proper file-level dedup), but that does not rule out the session-level leakage described above. These numbers must NOT be cited as evidence of shape or polymer classification capability in the STTR application without first addressing this via a product/session-held-out split.

trivial_dimension_only_baseline.description: RandomForest on [width, height, width/height] only, no pixel data, same split

robustness_swin_t: See robustness_results.json: 100% accuracy under all perturbations (flip, brightness, rotation +-15, contrast) -- zero degradation, consistent with shortcut learning rather than genuine morphology sensitivity.
